rationale: C04 is the immediately preceding Citizenship Day proclamation and supplies a concrete, material template for the child. The two proclamations share nearly identical statutory recitals and the same distinctive three-part operative sequence: government and private flag displays, ceremonies organized by the same enumerated groups, and a call for citizens to renew and reaffirm allegiance to constitutional principles. The child primarily updates the date and revises the commemorative language while retaining C04's structure and much of its wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas, by joint resolution approved February 29, 1952 (66 Stat. 9), the Congress ... has designated the 17th day of September of each year as Citizenship Day ... in recognition of all our citizens who have come of age and all who have been naturalized during the year
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas, by joint resolution approved February 29, 1952 (66 Stat. 9), the Congress ... has designated the 17th day of September of each year as Citizenship Day ... in recognition of all our citizens who have come of age and all who have been naturalized during the year
shared_material.explanation: The opening statutory recital is essentially verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do call upon the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag ... on all Government buildings on Monday, September 17, 1956, and urge the people ... to display the flag on that day at their homes and other suitable places
shared_material.parent_excerpt: call upon the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag ... on all Government buildings on Saturday, September 17, 1955, and urge the people ... to display the flag on that day at their homes and other suitable places
shared_material.explanation: The principal operative direction is copied with only the annual date changed and a minor grammatical adjustment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also urge Federal, State, and local officials, as well as religious, civic, patriotic, educational, and other organizations, to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also urge Federal, State and local officials, as well as religious, civic, patriotic, educational, and other organizations, to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day
shared_material.explanation: The same enumerated organizers and ceremony mechanism appear in the same position.

shared_material.child_excerpt: And I also call upon all our citizens to renew and reaffirm their fealty on that day to the principles embodied in the Constitution—the foundation of our free and independent Republic.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: And I also call upon all our citizens to renew and reaffirm their allegiance on that day to the principles and ideals embodied in the Constitution—the foundation of our strength and the symbol of freedom and justice for all.
shared_material.explanation: The final operative paragraph preserves the distinctive renew-and-reaffirm formulation and constitutional-foundation construction while revising the concluding description.
